Causation.description: Why this event exists: the chain it belongs to and the event that caused it.

hop.description: 0 for a root event, parent hop + 1 otherwise.

parent.description:
The id of the event whose handler proposed the change that produced
this one. Absent for a root event, never spelled `null` on the wire:
the decoder refuses bytes a re-encode cannot reproduce. A UUID when
present.

root.description:
The id of the first event in the chain; equals `id` for a root event.
A later orchestrator correlates on this field. A UUID, like every
event identity on the envelope.

EventSubject.description: The product record the triggering change landed on.

recordReference.description: The record reference, as the product addresses it.

recordRevision.description:
The revision the triggering change produced. Revisions start at one, so
a revision of zero or below is refused on both encode and decode, the
same bound the delivery store enforces on a stored envelope.

HookEnvelope.description: The hook envelope, one shape for every product and every destination kind.

causation.description: The chain this event belongs to.

data.description:
The product projection. Integers that are not exactly representable as
binary64 must be strings; canonical JSON refuses them otherwise.

dataschema.description: The product data contract id for `data`.

id.description:
Event identity, unique per triggering change. The idempotency key a
remote handler must honor across retries.

A UUID: the delivery store keys an envelope by a UUID event id, so an
id that is not one could never be stored. Refused on both encode and
decode.

source.description: The producing product and deployment identity.

subject.description: The product record reference and revision.

time.description:
Commit time of the triggering change, RFC 3339.

Normalized on every serialization: converted to UTC and truncated to
whole milliseconds, so two equal instants written at different offsets
or at finer precision produce identical canonical bytes. The in-memory
value keeps whatever the product gave it; the wire form is the
normalized one. Decoding requires that wire form and refuses any other
spelling, so a decoded envelope re-encodes to the bytes it arrived as.

reviewPolicy.description: Exact Review policy binding when this workflow exposes the Review protocol; otherwise null.

eventSource.description: The platform v1 HMAC delivery signature, bound to the canonical envelope, signed delivery headers, HTTP method and exact request target. The configured event source key is separate from caller bearer tokens.
